The one analytics file with no size bound

Ten analytics files respect a 10 MB cap for free. One does not, because it is written by the dispatcher rather than by appendAnalytics().

300 MBhook-timing.jsonl
30×over the 10 MB cap
~730 MBper year, unbounded
0rotations ever fired

Why only this file

every other analytics file
  hook  ──▶  appendAnalytics()  ──▶  rotateIfNeeded()  ──▶  append   bounded ✓

hook-timing.jsonl
  run-hook.mjs  ──────────────────────────────────▶  appendFile()   unbounded ✗
       └─ a plain .mjs dispatcher: runs before/outside the compiled TS
          bundles, so it cannot import the helper and appends raw.

Measured

FileSizevs 10 MB cap

The siblings are not under the cap because rotation trimmed them. They are under it because they are genuinely small. No analytics file has ever rotated — which is exactly why a 30× outlier went unnoticed: nothing on disk looked unusual.

The fix

src/hooks/bin/run-hook.mjs
  const timingPath = join(analyticsDir, 'hook-timing.jsonl');
+ rotateAnalyticsIfNeeded(timingPath);
  appendFile(timingPath, ...)
The helper is duplicated from lib/analytics.ts rather than imported, because the dispatcher cannot reach the TS bundles. Same cap, same .YYYY-MM.jsonl naming, same swallow-all-errors contract, so behaviour stays identical across all eleven files. Cost is one statSync per invocation against an appendFile that already happened.
